person.summary: AI Engineer and Researcher based in Rio de Janeiro. I am a PhD student in Applied Mathematics and Data Science at FGV EMAp, where I completed my MSc and work with the Visual Data Science Lab on urban video understanding, vision-language models, agentic retrieval and visual analytics. My first-author paper, UrbanClipAtlas, was published in Computer Graphics Forum and presented at EuroVis 2026, I have co-authored papers at SIBGRAPI 2025 and 2026, and I first-authored HopViz for the IEEE VAST Challenge 2026. I also build the systems that carry this research into production: Django/DRF and React/TypeScript services running on Docker and Kubernetes.

primaryRoles: Researcher — Visual Analytics & Urban Video Understanding
differentiators: Three peer-reviewed publications: first author of UrbanClipAtlas (Computer Graphics Forum, EuroVis 2026), co-author of STRive (Computers & Graphics, SIBGRAPI 2025) and of a SIBGRAPI 2026 paper comparing monocular and multi-view 3D pedestrian reconstruction at urban intersections. Plus two IEEE VAST Challenge 2026 entries: HopViz (first author) and AgentAudit.
Research prototypes built to survive production — Django/DRF, React/TypeScript, Docker and Kubernetes, with CI/CD.
End-to-end ownership: architecture, implementation, interface and deployment, from paper figure to running service.

proofPoints.claim: Reduced time spent on key operational processes by 90% through Python automation.
Integrated CRM/ERP, LMS, and messaging channels into end-to-end workflows.
Microservices and CI/CD architecture for reliable, scalable deployments.

projects.title: UrbanClipAtlas: A Visual Analytics Framework for Event and Scene Retrieval in Urban Videos
projects.venue: Computer Graphics Forum, vol. 45, no. 3 (Proc. EuroVis 2026)
projects.presentedAt: Presented at EuroVis 2026 — Nottingham, UK — June 2026
projects.description: A visual analytics system for exploring long urban videos recorded at street intersections. It segments recordings into clips, describes them with a vision-language model and indexes them for semantic retrieval, combining retrieval-augmented generation with taxonomy-aware entity extraction and video grounding. A knowledge graph aligns the language model output with detected objects and trajectories, so every answer can be visually grounded and verified. Evaluated on the StreetAware dataset through case studies on hazardous scenarios and pedestrian crossing dynamics.
projects.summary: Ask questions of hours of street-intersection video and get answers grounded in what the cameras tracked.

image.alt: UrbanClipAtlas interface: chat panel with entity tooltips, video player with tracking overlays, related-clips timeline

projects.title: Comparing Monocular and Multi-View 3D Pedestrian Reconstruction Strategies for Urban Intersection Sensing
projects.venue: Proc. SIBGRAPI 2026 — Conference on Graphics, Patterns and Images
projects.description: Compares a monocular learned pipeline (text-prompted segmentation, tracking and learned 3D body estimation) with a calibrated multi-view geometric pipeline (2D pose, tracking, cross-camera association and triangulation) for deriving pedestrian motion descriptors at urban intersections. Without 3D ground truth, it evaluates coverage, anthropometric plausibility, walking-speed distributions, compute cost and failure modes, and gives practical guidance on when to use each.
projects.summary: Monocular vs. multi-view 3D pedestrian reconstruction at intersections, compared without 3D ground truth.

image.alt: Side-by-side pipelines: monocular learned (4 steps) vs multi-view geometric (4 steps) for 3D pedestrian pose

projects.title: STRive: An association rule-based system for the exploration of spatiotemporal categorical data
projects.description: A system for mining and exploring association rules over spatiotemporal categorical data. It pairs rule generation and rule clustering with an interactive interface offering two analysis modes — one at the cluster level, one at the individual rule level — connected through coordinated views. Demonstrated through case studies on fatal vehicle accidents and urban crime.
projects.summary: Mines and clusters association rules in spatiotemporal data, explored through coordinated map and heatmap views.

image.alt: STRive interface: control panel, cluster scatterplot, US map, attribute and heatmap views, plus an LLM explanation panel

projects.title: HopViz: Tracing Anomalous Behaviour Hop-By-Hop Through a Tangled Multi-Agent System
projects.description: A browser-based visual analytics tool that explains an anomalous gibberish post in the Tenant Thread multi-agent system. From a 185,147-event log of human, agent and system activity, it combines a single-screen overview of nine coordinated panels with an on-demand causal tracing engine. It reveals the post as the final hop of a worm-like instruction file propagating agent-to-agent, and identifies the single authorization gateway that would prevent it.
projects.summary: Traces an anomalous post through 185,147 agent events to a worm-like file and the one gateway that stops it.

image.alt: HopViz single-screen dashboard: posts, timing and incident panels, causal chain timeline, schema, payload, chokepoint, actor panels

projects.title: AgentAudit: Visual Analytics for Tracing Behavioral Escalation in Multi-Agent Systems
projects.description: Reconstructs how autonomous agents escalate to a policy breach from their public posts, private deliberations and internal reasoning, coupling topic evolution, event extraction, per-agent channel usage and think-say dissonance. On the VAST Challenge 2026 data it traces an embargo breach to coordination migrating into private and anonymous channels, foreshadowed by dissonance from the earliest rounds.
projects.summary: Reconstructs how LLM agents drift into a policy breach, from topic shifts to the gap between thought and speech.

image.alt: AgentAudit dashboard: TopicRiver stream graph, per-topic word clouds, channel event timeline and agent message list

current.title: How do you search hours of street video, and trust the answer?
current.summary: My PhD at FGV EMAp continues the MSc thesis on visual analytics for long urban video. The work runs on three threads: retrieving the right clip, grounding every answer in what the cameras actually tracked, and measuring how people move through intersections.

threads.label: Retrieve
threads.text: Vision-language descriptions of short clips, indexed for retrieval-augmented question answering.

threads.label: Ground
threads.text: A knowledge graph that aligns each answer with detected objects and trajectories, so it can be checked frame by frame.

threads.label: Measure
threads.text: 3D pedestrian pose, stature and walking speed recovered from fixed intersection cameras.
